data={'answer': 'Salesforce uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication rather than traditional API keys [1][2][3]. To authenticate, you must configure an External Client App or a Connected App in your Salesforce org [1][4]. These apps provide a Consumer Key (client_id) and Consumer Secret (client_secret) used during the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow to obtain an access token [5][6]. Once authorized, you include this token in your API requests using the Authorization header [5]:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <Access_Token>
```

You must assign appropriate OAuth scopes to your app to define the level of access granted [7][5][2]. web_evidence.query: "Pipedrive" official developer documentation API authentication OAuth API key
web_evidence.result:
data={'answer': "Pipedrive supports two authentication methods: OAuth 2.0 for public and private apps, and a manual API token for simple integrations [1][2][3].

For OAuth 2.0, register your app in the Developer Hub to obtain a client_id and client_secret [4]. Use these to perform the OAuth flow via https://oauth.pipedrive.com to exchange an authorization code for an access_token and refresh_token [5]. Authenticate API requests by including the access_token in the Authorization header [6]:

```
GET https://{COMPANYDOMAIN}.pipedrive.com/api/v1/deals
-H 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>'
```

Alternatively, you can obtain a static API token manually from your Pipedrive account settings to authenticate requests [1][7]. For new projects, the create-pipedrive-app tool provides boilerplate code that includes the OAuth flow and API client setup [6][2][4].", 'citations': [{'id': 'https://developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1', 'title': '', 'url': 'https://developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1'}, {'id': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/getting-started', 'title': '', 'url': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/getting-started'}, {'id': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/marketplace-creating-a-proper-app', 'title': '', 'url': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/marketplace-creating-a-proper-app'}, {'id': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/developer-hub', 'image': 'https://files.readme.io/886affb57d00aa7f1b778b6f463ac5beca58b4ca53bc77a20e04302627f52bef-pipedrive-developers-og.png', 'title': 'Developer Hub', 'url': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/developer-hub'}, {'id': 'https://developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1/Oauth', 'title': '', 'url': 'https://developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1/Oauth'}, {'id': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/marketplace-oauth-api', 'image': 'https://files.readme.io/886affb57d00aa7f1b778b6f463ac5beca58b4ca53bc77a20e04302627f52bef-pipedrive-developers-og.png', 'title': 'OAuth 2.0 overview', 'url': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/marketplace-oauth-api'}, {'id': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/core-api-concepts-about-pipedrive-api', 'image': 'https://files.readme.io/886affb57d00aa7f1b778b6f463ac5beca58b4ca53bc77a20e04302627f52bef-pipedrive-developers-og.png', 'publishedDate': '2017-10-19T00:00:00.000Z', 'title': 'About the Pipedrive API', 'url': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/core-api-concepts-about-pipedrive-api'}, {'id': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/core-api-concepts-requests', 'image': 'https://files.readme.io/886affb57d00aa7f1b778b6f463ac5beca58b4ca53bc77a20e04302627f52bef-pipedrive-developers-og.png', 'title': 'Requests', 'url': 'https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/core-api-concepts-requests'}]} error=None log_id='log_IDXWvJ0V23U4'

web_evidence.result: data={'answer': 'To access the Pipedrive API, you must register your app in the Developer Hub to obtain a client ID and client secret, which are required for OAuth 2.0 authentication. Content-Type: application/json

{

}

For the TypeScript SDK, use the close method on your McpServer or Server instance [1][2]. When using stdio, the server should also exit promptly when its standard input is closed [4].

```typescript
// Example for TypeScript SDK
await server.close();
```

For HTTP transports, calling close on the handler aborts in-flight requests and closes the connection [3]. In the Kotlin SDK, use the suspendable close function [5]. data={'answer': 'Copper provides two primary methods for API access: OAuth 2.0 for third-party integrations and legacy API Keys for direct authentication [1][2].

To use OAuth 2.0, you must register your application by emailing partners@copper.com to receive a client_id and client_secret [1]. This flow uses the Authorization Code Grant, requiring your application to exchange a temporary code for an access token [1].

For legacy API Keys, generate credentials via the Copper Platform UI under Organisation settings [2]. When using these keys, include the following headers in your HTTPS requests [3]:

```http
X-PW-AccessToken: <API_Key>
X-PW-Application: developer_api
X-PW-UserEmail: <Email_address_of_token_owner>
Content-Type: application/json
```

The Developer API base URL is https://api.copper.com/developer_api/ [4]. data={'answer': 'There is no single official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provided by Copper CRM. Several third-party solutions exist to connect Copper CRM to AI assistants:

CData offers a Python-based MCP server and an API Driver for MCP that provide SQL-based access to Copper data [1][2]. StackOne provides a hosted Copper MCP server featuring 58 pre-built actions with managed authentication [3]. Aerostack also hosts a Copper MCP server that provides a single URL for integration with various AI agents [4]. Additionally, there is an unofficial, read-heavy demo server available on GitHub [5] and a managed service via MCPBundles [6].

data={'answer': 'DealCloud uses OAuth2 Client Credentials for API authentication [1][2]. To authenticate, send a POST request to the token endpoint to receive a bearer token, which must be included in the Authorization header of subsequent requests [1].

Endpoint: {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token [1]

Example request:
```
POST {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

scope=data user_management
&grant_type=client_credentials
&client_id=your_client_id
&client_secret=your_client_secret
```

Tokens expire after 15 minutes [1]. You can obtain your API credentials by enabling the API in your user profile settings under Admin > User Management [3]. The Inbox API uses OAuth 2.0 with Authorization Code or Client Credentials flows. You must create an app in your profile to generate an application ID and secret.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.helpscout.net/v2/oauth2/token \
    --data "grant_type=client_credentials" \
    --data "client_id={application_id}" \
    --data "client_secret={application_secret}"
```

The Docs API uses API Key authentication via HTTP Basic Auth, where the key serves as the username and a dummy value serves as the password.

```bash
curl --user {api_key}:X https://docsapi.helpscout.net/v1/collections
```

web_evidence.query: "Lark (Larksuite)" official developer documentation API authentication OAuth API key
web_evidence.result:
data={'answer': 'Lark (Larksuite) uses the Open Platform for API authentication, primarily relying on App ID and App Secret to obtain access tokens [1][2][3].

For server-to-server communication, use the Tenant Access Token. Obtain it by sending a POST request to the internal authentication endpoint [4][1]:

```http
POST https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal
Content-Type: application/json

{
    "app_id": "YOUR_APP_ID",
    "app_secret": "YOUR_APP_SECRET"
}
```

Include the returned `tenant_access_token` in the Authorization header as a Bearer token for subsequent API calls [4][1].

For user-specific actions, use OAuth 2.0 [2][5]. Configure your redirect URL and scopes in the Lark Developer Console under your app's security settings [2][6][5]. The flow involves exchanging an authorization code for a `user_access_token` and optionally an `offline_access` refresh token [2][6][5]. Official documentation and SDKs are available via the Lark Open Platform [2][7].', 'citations': [{'id': 'https://github.com/nehsus/glark', 'title': 'nehsus/glark', 'url': 'https://github.com/nehsus/glark'}, {'id': 'https://github.com/ariesho2903/n8n-nodes-lark-global', 'title': 'ariesho2903/n8n-nodes-lark-global', 'url': 'https://github.com/ariesho2903/n8n-nodes-lark-global'}, {'id': 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/lark-openclaw', 'title': 'lark-openclaw', 'url': 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/lark-openclaw'}, {'id': 'https://docs.rs/crate/agentzero-channels/latest/source/src/channels/lark.rs', 'title': 'agentzero-channels 0.3.0 - Docs.rs', 'url': 'https://docs.rs/crate/agentzero-channels/latest/source/src/channels/lark.rs'}, {'id': 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-feishu-lark', 'title': 'n8n-nodes-feishu-lark', 'url': 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-feishu-lark'}, {'id': 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-feishu-api', 'title': 'n8n-nodes-feishu-api', 'url': 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-feishu-api'}, {'id': 'https://crates.io/crates/larksuite-oapi-sdk-rs', 'title': 'larksuite-oapi-sdk-rs', 'url': 'https://crates.io/crates/larksuite-oapi-sdk-rs'}, {'id': 'https://github.com/larksuite/openclaw-lark/', 'title': 'larksuite/openclaw-lark', 'url': 'https://github.com/larksuite/openclaw-lark/'}]} error=None log_id='log_HK9KqOxoyK4V'

For API requests, use the following base endpoint structure:
`https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/` [7][4]

Example for obtaining a tenant access token:
```json
POST https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal
{
    "app_id": "your_app_id",
    "app_secret": "your_app_secret"
}
```

To access the Telegram API, register your application at https://my.telegram.org to obtain an api_id and api_hash. For the Bot API, create a bot via @BotFather to receive an authentication token. For the Gateway API, register at the gateway platform, fund your account, and generate an access token.

```python
# Example: Gateway API request
import requests
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_TOKEN'}
data = {'phone_number': '+1234567890'}

Use Basic Authentication for private integrations or internal tools connected to your own Aircall account [1][2]. Generate an API ID and API Token in your Aircall Dashboard under Integrations > API Keys [2][3]. Authenticate by sending a Base64-encoded string of `api_id:api_token` in the Authorization header [2][4].

```http
Authorization: Basic <BASE64_ENCODED_CREDENTIALS>
```

Use OAuth for applications serving multiple customers or those intended for the Aircall App Marketplace [1][2]. This flow requires a Client ID and Client Secret obtained from Aircall [5][2]. You must exchange an authorization code for a permanent access token via a POST request to `https://api.aircall.io/v1/oauth/token`, which is then used as a Bearer token [5][2].

Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>

For OAuth 2.0, GoHighLevel uses the Authorization Code grant flow [2][1]. Developers register their application in the Developer Marketplace to obtain a Client ID and Client Secret [3]. The process involves redirecting the user to an authorization URL, receiving an authorization code, and exchanging that code via a POST request to the /OAuth/token endpoint for an access and refresh token [3][2].

For API Keys, GoHighLevel allows for authentication via API Key or Basic Auth, which are configured in the app settings and sent with each request [1].

Official SDKs for PHP, Python, and TypeScript/JavaScript are available to automate these flows, including token storage and automatic refreshing [4][5][6][7]. data={'answer': 'Mailchimp provides two primary authentication methods for its Marketing API: API keys and OAuth 2 [1].

Use an API key if you are writing code that tightly couples your application to your own Mailchimp account [1][2]. Generate keys in the API Keys section of your account [3]. Authenticate using HTTP Basic Auth with any string as the username and your key as the password [1]:

```bash
curl --request GET \
--url 'https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/' \
--user 'anystring:YOUR_API_KEY'
```

Use OAuth 2 for third-party integrations where you need to access other users' accounts [1][2]. This requires registering your application to obtain a client ID and secret [2]. The flow involves redirecting users to Mailchimp to authorize access, exchanging a temporary code for an access token, and using that token with the OAuth Metadata endpoint to retrieve the user's data center prefix [2]. Authenticate requests using the Bearer header [1]:

```bash
curl --request GET \
--url 'https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/' \
--header "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>"
```', 'citations': [{'id': 'https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/fundamentals/', 'image': data={'answer': 'Systeme.io provides a Public API that uses API keys for authentication [1][2]. You can generate these keys by navigating to your profile settings and selecting the MCP & API keys section [2][3].

To authenticate your requests, include your API key in the X-API-Key header [1][4]. While some documentation mentions OAuth 2.0 for integrations [5], the official developer reference currently specifies the X-API-Key header as the primary method for the Public API [1][4].

Example using cURL:
```bash
curl -X POST 'https://api.systeme.io/api/tags' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H 'X-API-Key: your_api_key' \
-d '{"name": "NewTagName"}'
```

Example using JavaScript:
```javascript
fetch('https://api.systeme.io/api/contacts', {
    headers: {
        'X-API-Key': 'your_api_key'
    }
})
.then(response => response.json())
.then(data => console.log(data));
```

Always perform API calls from a secure server-side environment to protect your key [1]. web_evidence.result: data={'answer': 'The Threads API is a freemium service that allows developers to build integrations for publishing content, managing replies, and accessing analytics [1][2][3]. data={'answer': 'Twilio SendGrid uses API keys for authentication rather than OAuth or username/password combinations [1][2]. You must include your API key in the Authorization header of your requests using the Bearer token format [1][2].

To authenticate, pass the following header with your API calls:
Authorization: Bearer <Your-API-Key-Here>

Example using cURL:
```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_HERE' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"personalizations":[{"to":[{"email":"recipient@example.com"}]}],"from":{"email":"sender@example.com"},"subject":"Hello","content":[{"type":"text/plain","value":"World"}]}'
```

You can generate and manage these keys in the SendGrid console under Settings > API Keys [1][3]. For security, SendGrid requires two-factor authentication (2FA) for all accounts and recommends storing your API key in an environment variable rather than hardcoding it [1][3][4].', 'citations': data={'answer': "There is no single official SendGrid MCP server provided by Twilio. Instead, there are several community-maintained implementations available for use with MCP-compatible clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Zed [1][2][3][4].

If you are looking to build your own, Twilio provides a developer guide for creating a custom MCP server using the FastMCP framework and the official SendGrid Python SDK [5].

For pre-built solutions, popular options include:

- deyikong/sendgrid-mcp: A widely used server providing 59 tools for email marketing, transactional operations, and analytics [1][3].
- justinritchie/mcp-sendgrid-server: A production-grade server focused on transactional email APIs with built-in safety features like read-only defaults, PII redaction, and write-approval tokens [4].
- sendgrid-mcp (by AnderEnder): A Rust-based implementation that exposes all 391 SendGrid v3 API operations through a meta-tool surface to avoid context bloat [2][6].

data={'answer': 'Shopify uses OAuth 2.0 to authorize apps and issue access tokens [1][2]. Your app's client credentials, referred to as the Client ID and Client Secret (or API Key and API Secret), are found in the Shopify Dev Dashboard [3][4]. These credentials are used to perform OAuth grants—such as authorization code, token exchange, or client credentials—to obtain an access token [5][2].

To authenticate API requests, include the access token in the request header [1][5]. For the GraphQL Admin API, use the `X-Shopify-Access-Token` header [1][6].

```http
POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id={your_client_id}
&client_secret={your_client_secret}
&grant_type=client_credentials
```

After obtaining the token, use it in your API calls [4][6]:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/api/2026-04/graphql.json \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Shopify-Access-Token: {YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN}' \
  -d '{"query": "query { shop { name } }"}'

web_evidence.result:
data={'answer': 'WooCommerce provides two primary methods for REST API authentication depending on your connection security [1][2].

For HTTPS connections, use HTTP Basic Auth by providing your Consumer Key as the username and Consumer Secret as the password [1][3]. If your server fails to parse the Authorization header, you may pass these credentials as query string parameters [4][5].

For non-SSL (HTTP) connections, you must use OAuth 1.0a "one-legged" authentication to prevent credential interception [1][6]. This requires generating a signature using the HMAC-SHA1 algorithm based on your Consumer Secret and specific OAuth parameters, including `oauth_consumer_key`, `oauth_timestamp`, `oauth_nonce`, and `oauth_signature_method` [2][3].

You can generate these keys manually via the WordPress admin under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API, or programmatically using the `/wc-auth/v1/authorize` endpoint [1][3].', 'citations': [{'id': 'https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/apis/rest-api/authentication/', 'image': 'https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/03/woo-dev-docs-banner.png', 'title': 'Authentication | WooCommerce developer docs', 'url': 'https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/apis/rest-api/authentication/'}, {'id': 'https://woocommerce.github.io/woocommerce-rest-api-docs/v3.html?php=', 'image': 'https://woocommerce.github.io/woocommerce-rest-api-docs/images/navbar-cad8cdcb.png', 'title': 'WooCommerce REST API Documentation v3', 'url': 'https://woocommerce.github.io/woocommerce-rest-api-docs/v3.html?php='}, {'id': 'https://woocommerce.github.io/woocommerce-rest-api-docs/?php=', 'title': 'WooCommerce REST API Documentation - ```bash
curl "https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/shopper/auth/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/oauth2/login" \

 -H "Authorization: Basic {Base64_Encoded_Credentials}" \
 -H "content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
 -d "grant_type=authorization_code_pkce&client_id={clientId}&code_challenge={challenge}&redirect_uri={uri}&channel_id={siteId}"
```

"Ecwid" official developer documentation API authentication OAuth API key
web_evidence.result:
data={'answer': 'Ecwid uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication. For custom apps managing your own store, you can skip the OAuth flow and retrieve access tokens directly from your app dashboard. For public or external apps, you must perform an OAuth handshake to exchange a temporary code for an access token via a POST request to the token endpoint.

All REST API requests must include the access token as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Passing tokens via query parameters is no longer supported.

Example request:

```http
GET /api/v3/{store_id}/profile HTTP/1.1
Host: app.ecwid.com
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

To exchange a code for an access token:

```http
POST /api/oauth/token HTTP/1.1
Host: my.ecwid.com

data={'answer': 'The Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API) uses Login with Amazon (LWA), an implementation of OAuth 2.0, for authentication [1][2]. You do not use a static API key; instead, you authenticate by exchanging your application credentials for an LWA access token [3][4].

To authenticate, you must first register your application to obtain a client_id and client_secret [3][4]. When a selling partner authorizes your application, you receive a refresh_token [3][4]. You exchange these credentials at the LWA token endpoint to receive an access_token [3][4]:

```http
POST https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=[your_refresh_token]&client_id=[your_client_id]&client_secret=[your_client_secret]
```

Include the returned access_token in the x-amz-access-token header for your API requests [3][4]. For restricted operations involving PII, use the Tokens API to generate a Restricted Data Token (RDT) instead [3][5].', 'citations': [{'id':   --header "Authorization: Basic ${cred}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json"
```

data={'answer': 'There are three distinct projects using the name Sherlock for the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

The first is an official server for the Covertlabs infostealer intelligence platform, which provides 12 tools for searching infostealer logs via a Personal Access Token [1][2][3]. It is built with FastMCP and supports stateless HTTP [2][3].

The second is a.NET-focused server (io.github.jcucci/dotnet-sherlock-mcp) that provides 36 tools for deep assembly introspection, including type hierarchy analysis, member searching, and XML documentation extraction [4][5]. It is installed as a global NuGet tool and communicates via stdio [4][5].

  --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --user "{CLIENT_ID}:{CLIENT_SECRET}"

```bash

data={'answer': 'Linear supports two primary authentication methods for its GraphQL API: personal API keys and OAuth 2.0 [1][2].

Personal API keys are recommended for individual scripts and can be managed in your account security settings [1][3]. Include them in your request header as follows [1]:

```http
Authorization: <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

OAuth 2.0 is recommended for applications intended for other users [1][4]. After completing the authorization flow, include the access token in your request header [1][4]:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
```

For server-to-server communication, Linear also supports the client_credentials grant type [4]. data={'answer': 'Asana provides two primary methods for API authentication: Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and OAuth 2.0 [1][2].

Personal Access Tokens function like traditional API keys [3][2]. They are the simplest method for personal scripts or quick testing and are generated via the Asana developer console [1][4]. Use them by passing the token in the Authorization header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

OAuth 2.0 is the recommended approach for applications that need to support multiple users [1][3]. It uses the authorization code grant flow [5]. Key endpoints include:

Authorization: `GET https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize` [5]
Token Exchange: `POST https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_token` [5]
Revocation: `POST https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_revoke` [5]

Applications must be registered in the developer console to obtain a client ID and client secret [5].', 'citations': [{'id': 'https://developers.asana.com/docs/authentication', 'publishedDate': Pricing models include feature-based and seat-based options, which are submitted via the Developer Center and reviewed by the team within 72 business hours [4][6]. data={'answer': 'Plaid uses a client ID and secret for API authentication, which you obtain from the Plaid Dashboard [1][2]. These credentials are required for almost all API requests and can be passed in the request body or via the PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET headers [1][3].

For OAuth-specific operations, Plaid provides dedicated endpoints like /oauth/token, /oauth/introspect, and /oauth/revoke [4]. These are used for service-to-service authentication and managing OAuth tokens, distinct from the end-user Link flow [4].

Example of authenticating an API call using headers:

```bash
curl 'https://sandbox.plaid.com/accounts/get' \
--header 'PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${YOUR_CLIENT_ID}' \
--header 'PLAID-SECRET: ${YOUR_SECRET}' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
  "access_token": "access-sandbox-..."
}'
```

web_evidence.result:
data={'answer': 'There is an official QuickBooks Online MCP server maintained by Intuit, alongside several community-developed alternatives.

The official Intuit project is a local, TypeScript-based server that provides comprehensive coverage of the QuickBooks Online API, including 29 entity types, 144 tools, and 11 financial reports [1][2]. It is designed for developers to build AI workflows against sandbox or production environments using OAuth 2.0 [2].

To use the official server, you must register an app on the Intuit Developer Portal to obtain a Client ID and Secret [1][2]. Because production environments require a public HTTPS callback for the initial OAuth handshake, developers often use tools like ngrok during setup [1][2]. Once authenticated, the server runs locally as a stdio subprocess [1][2].

Community alternatives include:
* @mindstone/mcp-server-quickbooks: A Node.js-based server that supports one-click configuration and includes a safety gate for mutating operations [3].
* mcp-quickbooks: A Python-based server using FastMCP that supports OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and provides both stdio and HTTP transport modes [4].
* qbo-mcp: A Node.js-based server that organizes tools into domains for easier navigation [5].

For agentic experiences where the LLM orchestrates complex workflows, Intuit also offers a hosted MCP server pilot program that requires onboarding through an Intuit Solution Engineer [6].', 'citations': [{'id': 'https://github.com/intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server', 'title': 'intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server', 'url': 'https://github.com/intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server'}, {'id': 'https://growthengineer.ai/mcp-servers/quickbooks-online', 'title': 'QuickBooks Online MCP Server - data={'answer': 'The PitchBook API does not use OAuth [1]. Instead, it uses a static API key provided by your PitchBook account team as part of a paid, contract-gated add-on [2][3][1]. To authenticate, you must include the API key in the Authorization header of every request using the format PB-Token {API_KEY} [3][1][4].

Base URL: https://api.pitchbook.com [2][3]

Example request:
```http
GET https://api.pitchbook.com/{route}

data={'answer': "Fathom supports two primary authentication methods: API keys and OAuth 2.0 [1][2].

data={'answer': 'The Devin API uses a principal-based authentication model requiring a token in the Authorization header of every request [1]. You should use a Service User API key for automated integrations, which are generated in your organization or enterprise settings and begin with the `cog_` prefix [1][2][3]. Personal Access Tokens (PATs) are also available for human programmatic access under your own identity [1][2]. Legacy API keys (`apk_` or `apk_user_` prefixes) are deprecated and should be replaced with service user tokens [1][4].

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.devin.ai/v3/organizations/$DEVIN_ORG_ID/sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer cog_your_token_here"
